rationale: Engineering and DevOps teams at companies using AI-powered dev tools are the buyer — these are named business roles with security budgets, and the Warp breach shows real, immediate financial and legal exposure. Adjacent paid tools (GitGuardian, Trufflesecurity) confirm willingness to pay for secret-scanning. However, the core delivery component requires meaningful integration work (hooking into agent trace pipelines, maintaining scanners per tool), and ongoing autonomy depends on how well-scoped the product is — a fully self-serve scanner SaaS is possible but non-trivial. The `buildability_with_ai` gate is borderline at 5, capping stage at validate until a concrete scoped MVP is proven.
solution_plan: A secrets-scrubbing and audit service for AI agent trace outputs — think a lightweight API or CLI wrapper that accepts agent log/trace data and returns a redacted version plus a risk report flagging any detected secrets (API keys, tokens, connection strings). The factory builds this as a Claude-powered detection prompt (using regex + LLM pattern recognition) behind a simple web intake form and a Stripe subscription link; the operator approves the initial outreach batch to security-conscious dev teams. Sell by reaching DevSecOps leads and engineering managers at companies actively using Warp, Cursor, or similar tools — find them via LinkedIn and communities like DevSecOps Slack or relevant GitHub repos. Billing and report delivery are automated; the only recurring human touch is approving outreach sends and any refund requests. Solo build+run is realistic if scoped to a self-serve report/API product, but integrating as an in-tool plugin for each AI dev tool would exceed solo capacity.
notes: buildability_with_ai at 5 is the binding constraint — real integration work required beyond a simple Claude prompt. Validate by shipping a self-serve web tool (paste trace → get redacted output + risk report) and testing paid conversion before investing in deeper integrations.
